partner_runtime.note: All six report live on /v1/stack. Search, Task, FindAll and Extract exercised in the Arm C run.

public_api.key_model: HMAC-signed stateless; verifies on every instance; never stored server-side

bring_your_own_data.retention: held in memory for the request only; never written to disk, logged, retained, or used for training

evaluation.media_served: development only; holdout returns 423 on every path

control_arm_ablation.note: The control declined correctly on both fragments where no identification is possible, contradicting the assumption the ablation was built to test; that result is published unchanged. The failure it does show is instability and unsourceability.

arm_b_control_plus_gate.note: The control's own answers through the production evidence builder and IdentityGate with an empty citation registry. Needs no partner credential. Shows the gate refuses unsourced claims; cannot show whether real evidence lifts a case above the threshold.

arm_c_full_system.miss: D04 abstained; ten citations rejected for paraphrase or live-page absence

assets.source: Library of Congress National Screening Room
assets.rights: United States public domain; all works published by 1929
assets.credit: Library of Congress, Motion Picture, Broadcasting, and Recorded Sound Division.

sources: The FIAF Moving Image Cataloguing Manual, Linda Tadic (ed.), FIAF, 2016
standards_conformance.finding: FIAF A.2.5 requires an unidentifiable entity still receive a supplied/devised title. Abstention previously returned no title; app/devised_title.py now supplies one.
standards_conformance.limitation: No archivist has reviewed this system. Conformance testing is weaker evidence than a practitioner review and is not a substitute for one.

practitioner_review.statement: No archivist has reviewed this system. Rather than leave that as a caveat, the project publishes a register of demands taken verbatim from published sources and answers each one, including two it cannot answer.
practitioner_review.primary_source: Abele, Anders, Aydin, Buder, Fischer, Kimmel and Huff, 'ArchiveGPT: A human-centered evaluation of using a vision language model for image cataloguing', arXiv:2507.07551 (2025); Humanities and Social Sciences Communications (2026). A peer-reviewed study in which archive and archaeology experts evaluated machine-generated catalogue descriptions.
practitioner_review.method: Sources were retrieved using this project's own Parallel Search surface, which reached pages an ordinary scripted fetch could not. Quotations are verbatim. Nobody cited has seen this system or endorses it.
behavioural_claims_executed: P1: `probable` is unreachable without human approval - asserted against the real gate.
P7: a claim with no source cannot carry a threshold - asserted against the real gate.

impact_case.survival: 14% of ~11,000 American silent feature films survive in original format; 5% of survivors incomplete; 26% found abroad. David Pierce, 'The Survival of American Silent Feature Films: 1912-1929', CLIR / Library of Congress for the National Film Preservation Board, December 2013.
impact_case.human_baseline: The Library of Congress 'Mostly Lost' identification workshop identified 23% (2016), 29% (2017) and 30% (2018) of the titles it screened during each event.
impact_case.comparison_disclaimer: Cited as context, not as a scoreboard. The corpora are not comparable, n=5 supports no rate, and no claim to outperform expert archivists is made anywhere in this project.

dossier_archive.statement: Complete, unedited responses captured from real runs of the deployed service, so the product can be read without waiting four to seven minutes for a run. Rendered by the same renderer a live run uses. Held-out cases are never captured.

measured_latency.note: The run console's stage timings were originally written from a pre-credential estimate totalling 100 seconds and were 4x optimistic. Corrected, and bound to the measurement by tests/test_published_latency_is_honest.py.
